newsitem.title: USA: McDonnell Douglas sees no restucturing.
newsitem.headline: McDonnell Douglas sees no restucturing.

text.p: McDonnell Douglas Corp chief executive officer Harry Stonecipher said Monday the company is not considering a major restructuring after the Defense Department eliminated the company from the race to build a new generation fighter jet.
"We don't see a restructuring at all," Stonecipher said in an interview on CNBC financial television network.
Stonecipher did say the St. Louis-based aerospace company continues to evaluate mergers and acquisitions.
"We've always been interested in mergers and acquisitions and we continue to look at them," he said.
McDonnell Douglas had reportedly had preliminary merger discussions with Boeing Co earlier this year. Stonecipher would not comment on any specific mergers or acquisitions.
"I don't think Boeing would be on our radar screen," he said regarding a possible acquisition. "We may be on their's."

Stonecipher also he would "absolutely" be interested in trading McDonnell Douglas's commercial aircraft assets for Boeing's military aircraft business, but added that there have not been discussions in that area.
"No there aren't. No there weren't," Stonecipher said of talks to swap assets with Boeing.
Boeing earlier Monday said it does not comment on rumors or speculation on mergers or acquisitions.

Boeing and Lockheed Martin Corp were chosen over a group including McDonnell Saturday to develop prototype fighter jets for the early 21st century for the U.S. Air Force, Navy, Marine Corps and British Royal Navy.
Analysts said the move could force McDonnell Douglas to consider a merger or restructuring or become more agressive in acquisitions.
Among the potential acquisitions is the defense electronics business of Texas Instruments Inc, which is for sale, according to published reports.
"Texas Instruments is a very interesting property if it in fact it is for sale," Stonecipher said in response to a question about Texas Instruments' electronics business.
Stonecipher said the company was not considering a restructuring and said the 200 people it had working on the fighter project were being reassigned Monday.
He would not say whether the company would seek business on the fighter project as a subcontractor.
"I think we have plenty of time to think about that," he said. "I don't plan to make those decisions anytime soon."
